target_moa.text: Prucalopride is a selective serotonin type 4 (5-HT4) receptor agonist, a GI prokinetic agent that stimulates colonic peristalsis (increasing bowel motility) and accelerates colonic transit.

citations.quote: Prucalopride, a selective serotonin type 4 (5-HT4) receptor agonist, is a gastrointestinal (GI) prokinetic agent that stimulates colonic peristalsis by increasing bowel motility.
It has motility stimulating properties in the GI tract with pronounced effects in the large intestine, where it stimulates peristalsis and accelerates colonic transit.

modality.text: Small molecule (new molecular entity, oral tablet)

citations.quote: Motegrity (prucalopride), a 5-HT4 receptor agonist, is a new molecular entity proposed for oral treatment of CIC in adults.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥2%) were headache (19% vs 9% placebo), abdominal pain (16% vs 11%), nausea (14% vs 7%), diarrhea (13% vs 5%), abdominal distension, dizziness, vomiting, flatulence, and fatigue. Suicidal ideation and behavior events were reviewed as a potential class issue and included in Warnings and Precautions.

citations.quote: The adequacy of the safety database was discussed during a public Gastrointestinal Advisory Committee (GIDAC) meeting on October 18, 2018. requirement.text: 3529-1: Evaluate the pharmacokinetics, efficacy, and safety of Motegrity in pediatric patients 6 months to less than 18 years of age with CIC via a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel group, 12-week treatment study (deferred pediatric study under PREA).

citations.quote: 3529-1 Evaluate the pharmacokinetics, efficacy, and safety of Motegrity (prucalopride) in pediatric patients with chronic idiopathic constipation (CIC) who are 6 months to less than 18 years of age by performing a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel group, 12-week treatment study.

requirement.text: 3529-2: Assess the long-term safety of Motegrity in pediatric patients 6 months to less than 18 years of age with CIC who completed a confirmatory efficacy/safety study, via an active comparator-controlled safety and tolerability study (deferred pediatric study under PREA).

citations.quote: 3529-2 Assess the long-term safety of Motegrity (prucalopride) in pediatric patients with chronic idiopathic constipation (CIC) who are 6 months to less than 18 years of age and have completed a confirmatory efficacy and safety study with Motegrity (prucalopride) by performing an active comparator-controlled safety and tolerability study.

requirement.text: 3529-3: A prospective, registry-based observational exposure cohort study comparing maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women exposed to Motegrity during pregnancy to an unexposed control population (505(o) requirement).

citations.quote: 3529-3 A prospective, registry based observational exposure cohort study that compares the maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women exposed to Motegrity (prucalopride) during pregnancy to an unexposed control population.
## **POSTMARKETING REQUIREMENTS UNDER 505(o)**

requirement.text: 3529-4: An additional pregnancy study using a different design from the Pregnancy Registry to assess major congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, small for gestational age, and preterm birth in women exposed to prucalopride during pregnancy (505(o) requirement).

citations.quote: 3529-4 An additional pregnancy study that uses a different design from the Pregnancy Registry (for example, a retrospective cohort study using claims or electronic medical record data with outcome validation or a case control study) to assess major congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, and small for gestational age and preterm birth in women exposed to Motegry (prucalopride) during pregnancy compared to an unexposed control population.
## **POSTMARKETING REQUIREMENTS UNDER 505(o)**

requirement.text: 3529-5: Perform a milk-only lactation trial in lactating women who received therapeutic doses of prucalopride, using a validated assay to assess prucalopride concentrations in breast milk and effects on the breastfed infant (505(o) requirement).

citations.quote: 3529-5 Perform a milk only lactation trial in lactating women who have received therapeutic doses of Motegry (prucalopride) using a validated assay to assess concentrations of prucalopride in breast milk and the effects on the breastfed infant.

summary.text: Standard (non-priority) review of NDA 210166, submitted under section 505(b) and received December 21, 2017 with a PDUFA goal date of 12/19/2018. A public Gastrointestinal Drugs Advisory Committee meeting held October 18, 2018 voted 10 to 0 in support of approval. Approved with deferred pediatric studies under PREA and postmarketing requirements; no accelerated approval, breakthrough, orphan, or fast track designation is stated.

citations.quote: Priority or Standard	Standard

Please refer to your New Drug Application (NDA) dated December 21, 2017, received December 21, 2017, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for Motegrity (prucalopride) 1 mg and 2 mg oral tablets.

The GIDAC voted 10 to 0 that the efficacy and safety of the clinical trial data, nonclinical findings, including the selectivity of prucalopride for the 5-HT4 receptor, and the results of the pharmacoepidemiology study included in the NDA are sufficient to support approval.

description.text: Updated Pediatric Use labeling to describe safety/efficacy results of a pediatric functional constipation study that was terminated early for futility, fulfilling postmarketing requirements (no new pediatric indication added)

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for updates to Section 8.4 *Pediatric Use* of the Prescribing Information to describe the safety and efficacy results of study TAK-555-3010, "Phase 3, Multicenter, Randomized Study with 2 Different Doses of Prucalopride Administered to Male and Female Pediatric Subjects Aged 6 Months to 17 Years with Functional Constipation, Consisting of a 12-week Double blind, Placebo-controlled Part (Part A) to Evaluate Efficacy and Safety Followed by a 36-week Double blind Extension (Part B) to Document Long-term Safety up to Week 48", which was conducted to fulfill postmarketing requirements 3529-1 and 3529-6, and terminated early for futility after the interim analysis indicated the study was unlikely to demonstrate effectiveness.
